extracted.intended_audience: CIA Office of Security staff, Office of Legislative Liaison, and agency policymakers reviewing/implementing OMB draft circular on federal law enforcement authorities
extracted.subtask_short: OMB circular review for federal law enforcement
extracted.subtask_description: Reviewing and assessing a draft OMB Circular titled 'Guidelines for Legislation Involving Federal Criminal Law Enforcement Authorities,' focusing on implications for agency authority, training/accreditation, firearms policy, and operational feasibility. The page is a memorandum from the Office of Security commenting on specific subsections of the draft circular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of protective responsibility under 40 U.S.C. 318
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the agency may accept delegation of protective responsibility under 40 U.S.C. 318 without further Congressional legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office of Security believes CIA 'has, in fact, such authority to accept protective authority without further Congressional legislation.' This criterion assesses if the draft guideline conflicts with or is unnecessary given existing statutory delegation (GSA to CIA memorandum of agreement, 6 February 1984).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to make a warrantless arrest — accredited training requirement (subsection 5(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsection 5(c) captioned 'Authority to Make a Warrantless Arrest' contains a caveat that the 'employee has completed an accredited course of training in the exercise of the power to arrest.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the guideline's training requirement is satisfied by agency training. The memo notes this guideline 'appears to preclude CIA in-house training for our ACOs and mandates external training at a law enforcement agency such as the FBI or the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center.' Consider implications for ACO program implementation and whether in-house accreditation would be acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'accredited course of training' (subsection 3(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsection 3(a) defines an accredited course of training as 'A systematic course of instruction by an appropriate Federal law enforcement agency.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to determine what constitutes acceptable accreditation; the definition implies courses must be provided by an 'appropriate Federal law enforcement agency,' which may exclude internal agency courses unless explicitly recognized. Assess whether the draft allows any flexibility (e.g., interagency accreditation or delegated instructor accreditation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to carry a firearm — accredited firearms training required (subsection 4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsection 4(a) 'Authority to Carry a Firearm' requires that officers who carry a firearm 'must complete an accredited course of training in the carrying and use of firearms.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether existing in-house firearms instruction meets the guideline's intent. The memo observes CIA historically used CIA instructors 'trained and accredited as a Firearms Instructor by the U.S. Secret Service' and questions if such in-house training 'meet[s] the spirit or the intent of the OMB guideline.' Consider whether external agency-led training or formal accreditation processes are required and the administrative burden of compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on Office of Security functions and authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of which Office of Security functions/authorities are affected by the draft circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memo identifies specific affected areas: 'appropriate legal responsibility to implement the Agency's new civilian guard force (tentatively termed "Access Control Officers" (ACOs))'; 'law enforcement training for the ACOs accreditation'; and 'CIA's authority to conduct firearms training.' Use these sub-elements to evaluate the draft's operational and legal impacts on agency missions and delegated responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational feasibility of external/centralized training and re-qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it is practical to require training and re-qualification to be accomplished by external Federal law enforcement agencies (centralized training).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memo warns that 'the sheer numbers of office of Security personnel involved in firearms training would make it impractical to train our personnel centrally at a single Federal law enforcement agency' and notes geographic dispersion of domestic field offices. Evaluate logistics, capacity, and cost implications; consider alternative approaches (distributed cooperation, reciprocal accreditation) to meet the guideline while remaining practical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to obtain expeditious legal opinion and designate inquiry point
rubrics_metrics.description: Need to secure prompt legal clarification about interpretation/impact of the draft guidelines and identify where inquiries should be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memo recommends 'you may wish to obtain an expeditious legal opinion on the draft guidelines' and instructs that 'inquiries regarding this matter should be addressed to [the] Policy and Plans Group.' Include a process for obtaining a legal determination and a clear point-of-contact for follow-up questions as part of implementing or responding to the draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing and record sheet procedural requirements for internal comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Format and procedural instructions for routing the draft within the agency and collecting officer comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scanned routing/record sheet shows fields such as SUBJECT, FROM, TO (Officer designation, room number, building), DATE, OFFICER'S COMMENTS (number each comment to show from whom RECEIVED FORWARDED INITIALS to whom), and instruction to 'Draw a line across column at., each comment.' Use this as the internal procedure for documenting and forwarding comments on the draft circular.
